articleTitle: Deep Learning for Native Advertisement Detection in Electronic News: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Native advertising is a type of commercial hybrid content that has successfully targeted online consumers. Native ads have become popular, especially on online platforms. People often don't realize that they are reading sponsored and paid content making native advertising very effective. Despite these benefits, native advertising has provoked strong negative responses, often accompanied by criticism and avoidance of the ads. This study aims to investigate the performance of different word embedding methods (BERT, GloVe, FastText) when used in combination with different deep learning methods (BiLSTM, CNN, LSTM) in detecting native ads in electronic news. The dataset used in this study was collected from the news portal, detik.com. Among these models, the BERT-BiLSTM model achieved the highest accuracy, f1 score, recall, precision and AUC score, all with the same value of 95%, compared to the other models, showing that the BERT-BiLSTM model outperformed the other models.

articleTitle: Analyzes of Chirps Spread Spectrum of ES920LR LoRa 920 MHz
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: One of the essential things in research using LoRa apart from the Internet of Things platform is that specific Chirps signals can be seen using a LoRa signal analyzer. Chirps is a type of signal in the form of Radar generated by LoRa during the communication process between LoRa at a certain frequency; in this research, using types of 920 MHz frequencies using the ES920LR type of LoRa, which is compatible in Japan. This research needs to be carried out in order to know the LoRa performance seen from the resulting Chirps signal, and in this research, the focus is to discuss the LoRa Chirps. In the current study, Chirps can be analyzed with MatLab programming. This research will compare signal chirps using MatLab programming and direct observations with Signal Analyzer; In conducting further studies, observations were made from the results of 2-way or more communication from the LoRa. And the possibility of analyzing the possible Symbol error rate of LoRa communication and the number sample of LoRa with various values of Spreading Factor (SF) and Bandwidth. Chirps Spread Spectrum (CSS) ES920LR LoRa is influenced by two critical parameters, i.e., Spreading Factor (SF) and Bandwidth (BW). The greater the Spreading Factor, the greater the number of samples produced starting from SF 7 with the number of samples generated being 250, SF 8 produces a number of samples 500, SF 9 produces a number of samples 1000, SF 10 produces number samples 2000, SF 11 produces number samples 4000, and SF12 produces a number of samples 8000. With a symbol error rate of 0.9-1

articleTitle: Adaptive Defense Scheme Implementation in Muarakarang Subsystem to Prevent Island Operation Failure
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Power system failures such as disturbances in generation, transmission lines, and other electrical equipment, may cause a large imbalance between power system supply and demand. Under certain conditions, disturbances such as in the interconnection network, the electric power system of a subsystem may be separated (island operation) by opening certain bays. To maintain the balance of the system, there is a mechanism called a defense scheme. This mechanism uses a conventional system protection mechanism, therefore the result able to overcome the problems. There is an advance mechanism in overcoming the problems of the electric power system called Adaptive Defense Scheme (ADS). This mechanism is dynamic, which means it able to read the loading and generation of a system in real time. In this study, the ADS PCS-992 Stability Controller implemented in Muarakarang subsystem has a crucial problem. The problem is island operation failure under certain disturbance conditions which causes blackouts in the subsystem. The total load saved with the island operation in scenario 1A is 1222 MW, scenario 1B is 1035 MW, and scenario 2A, 2B, 2C are 938 MW by installing ADS.

articleTitle: Increase in High Impedance Value of Transformer to Reduce Short Circuit Fault Currents in High Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Short-circuit current fault can have a bad impact on electric power systems that have high voltage levels. This adverse impact resulted in the burning of high-voltage equipment such as transformers. Several types of short circuit current faults that often occur in high voltage power systems such as line to ground, line to line, 2 lines to ground, and 3 phases. Circuit breakers can be a solution to disconnect the electric power system from short-circuit fault currents. In reality, there is still frequent damage to the transformer. The novelty of this research is to increase the high impedance of the transformer to reduce short-circuit fault currents in electric power systems that have high voltage levels. Several scenarios are made in order to be able to compare each change in transformer impedance to changes in short-circuit fault current. The first scenario increases the transformer impedance to 15% of its initial impedance. The second scenario increases the transformer impedance to 25%. Likewise for the third scenario the impedance increases to 35%. In the fourth scenario the impedance increase to 45%. Each scenario of increasing the value of the transformer impedance gives different results. Each scenario will be analyzed using a short circuit current measurement method at steady state. In addition, the fault current is also analyzed using the transient curve for the AC component, the DC component. The result is the lowest short-circuit fault current value occurs in the transformer with a high impedance percentage value of 45%. The higher the impedance value of the transformer, the lower the short-circuit fault current that occurs.

articleTitle: FPGA Displays Real-Time Video Camera on VGA Monitor
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The OV7670 camera module is 8 bits data image and it has a specification image of 30 frames per second. There are many applications of research that have been done about how to access this camera module and display it to the monitor. This paper presents the interface between this camera module OV7670 and FPGA DEO-Nano-Soc and then displays the video to the monitor via a VGA port. VGA port has a minimum of 5 pins; 3 pins for RGB data images, 1 pin for horizontal synchronous, and 1 pin for vertical synchronization. Due to the FPGA DE0-Nano-Soc not having the VGA driver, so the VGA driver ADV7133 24 bits is used in this research. The result showed that this research can work well enough. The system successfully to take the image from the camera and displays it as video in real-time.

articleTitle: A 30-Pointed Star-Shaped Patch Wideband Antenna for WLAN and WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Wideband microstrip antenna is required in modern wireless communication. Microstrip antenna has the characteristic of being lightweight, small in size, and easy-to-integrate. Due to the need for wideband antennas, many types of antenna patches have been developed over the years. In this work, a novel antenna of a 30-pointed star-shaped patch was designed to operate in WLAN and WiMAX bands and fabricated on an FR-4 substrate. The antenna bandwidths are 4.5 GHz in simulation and multiband of 0.9312 GHz and 2.946 GHz in measurement. Both simulation and measurement bandwidths cover the WLAN and WiMAX frequency bands.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Longitudinal and Lateral Dynamic of Autonomous Car
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Autonomous cars, when two essential variables influence tracks to determine their stability, namely position control and speed control. Speed is a control variable in longitudinal motion because it controls car movement along the X axis. Steering is a control variable in the lateral control system because it controls car movement along the Y axis. Some of the studies before, most of them only paid attention to one variable between speed and steering, and other variables are considered constant. Therefore, in this study, multivariable control was carried out using Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) to determine the speed and steering of the car. Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) predicts control inputs in the next few steps. The use of the predicted value results is to minimize the execution time required by the car control system. Because the system's complexity in autonomous cars is high, thus it is better to process data faster. The NMPC process produces a car's steering angle and speed value that must be achieved when tracking on a predetermined track. The results showed that the proposed control strategy could precisely set the vehicle to follow the target's trajectory.

articleTitle: Implementation of Busbar Protection at 150 kV Substations Based on IEC61850 Goose Message
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In electrical power installations, especially in high or extra high voltage installations, the role of the equipment protection system is vital to ensure the safety of the installation due to system faults. Busbar is the main part in substation which need to be protected. One of the protection schemes is bus bar protection (BBP) system. Ideally, every substation has busbar protection, but due to several reasons, often, the busbar protection at a substation is not installed or installed but inactive. To deal with that problem, GOOSE message is used to develop as BBP system. IEC61850 goose massage-based BBP can be implemented by designing specific additional logic and signal. Compared to BBP with the existing scheme, which are high impedance and low impedance types, this new system has several advantages, including operating flexibility, implementation time, and installation costs. Only the operating time has a slightly longer time than the usual system, where the GOOSE for BPP's operating time is 100ms, while the regular BBP is Oms. This method already implemented at Bekasi 150kV Substation and shows good stability in discriminating whether external or busbar fault. However, a new scheme can be an alternative solution for the absence of a BBP at a substation so that the bus bar protection system of the substation is still provided. With Busbar Protection based on GOOSE Message, busbar disturbances can be localized quickly, around 100ms. Thus, increasing the reliability of the busbar protection system and reducing the risk of widespread blackouts.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of Partial Shading Effects on the P-V Characteristic Curve
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Under natural conditions, solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays usually experience partial shadowing conditions (PSC), which can occur due to cloud shadows, passing birds or building shadows etc., which causes the P-V characteristics of solar cells to change from uniform solar radiation conditions. In uniform solar radiation, the P-V characteristic consists of only one Maximum Power Point (MPP) along with the functional operating voltage. However, partial shading conditions will give rise to complex P-V characteristics with several MPPs. So, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm may be trapped at the local peak, which is smaller than the global peak. In this paper, an investigation of the impact of partial shading conditions is carried out on photovoltaic arrays in the experiments. The experimental results show that the increase of partial shading creates additional peaks that grow gradually, in addition to that the initial peak decrease little by little. When the partial shading increase to 60%, the additional peak become a global peak since it is bigger than the initial peak. So, the global peak position of the characteristic curve shifted to another side of the curve, which is a challenge for MPPT method. By using the Global Maximum Power Point Detection (GMPPD) method proposed here, the global peak can still be found regardless of its position in any part of the characteristic curve.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Tracker Based PV Panel for Stand-Alone PV /Diesel/Battery Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In this paper, the PV/diesel/battery electrical power system for the community health center in the Mentawai Island has been presented with different tracking mechanisms. First, the health center's electrical system was designed for a photovoltaic (PV) system with fixed installations combined with diesel generators as backup systems. The optimal results with the lowest cost of energy (CoE) values are obtained with the operation of the PV /Diesel configuration and storage system. Furthermore, the electrical system was tested using three different PV structure installations - fixed structures, single-axis tracking, and dual-axis tracking mechanisms. Among the three tracking configurations, the two-axis tracking system was the most profitable in terms of PV electricity production of 3,931 kWh in a year and had the lowest CoE of 0.307 $/kWh. The payback period for a flat PV system is longer than the two-axis tracker PV system. Apart from the increase in power generation, PV systems with two-axis solar tracking will need fewer PV modules to supply the same load, requiring less space.

articleTitle: Optimization of 5G NR Network Based on Performance of 4G LTE Network in Area of Universitas Brawijaya Malang
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The demand and need for network services and mobile data services are very high, which encourages the use of 5G NR technology. Currently, 5G NR technology has not been fully implemented in Indonesia. As a result, a 5G NR MHz network planning was carried out in this study based on the performance of the 4G LTE network obtained from the drive test method in the area of Universitas Brawijaya, Malang. The coverage planning uses the cost-hatta propagation model. This propagation model is used with the consideration of flexible frequency usage, and the city of Malang is an urban area. The purpose of this study was to determine the site location mapping (gNodeB) and 5G NR network coverage at Universitas Brawijaya Malang. So the results can be taken into consideration in planning the 5G NR network. 5G NR network planning is created by calculate the cell radius, coverage, calculate the number of sites, and mapping them on a planning tool called Atoll.

articleTitle: Carbon Nanotubes, Graphite, and Reduced Graphene Oxide in CuSCN incorporated Carbon Electrodes in Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The efficiency of perovskite solar cells has been improved within the last thirteen years of development, bringing forth new innovations such as low-temperature processes, applicable low-budget raw materials, and shorter fabrication time. However, the electrode layering process still faces obstacles such as having high price, rapid degradation, and complex fabrication. In response to this, carbon materials are becoming more attractive in the development of solar cell electrodes because of their high conductivity values. Many previous studies have been conducted to obtain the best photovoltaic performance with various carbon materials. However, there has been no research into the performance of perovskite solar cell (PSC) with counter electrodes made from a mix of hole transport materials and various carbon-based materials. In this research, it is proposed an attempt to combine CuSCN as a hole transport material with different carbon materials such as graphite, reduced graphene oxide, and carbon nanotubes (CNT). The CuSCN and carbon material were combined with the ball milling process and they are deposited with the doctor blading method. After that, the perovskite solar cell performance was measured. The device's best performance was obtained from PSC with an electrode made from CNT and CuSCN, which shows Isc, Voc, and FF of 0.4489 mA, 0.52 V, and 0.3691, respectively.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of USRP N210 as Simple GSM OpenBTS 5.0 for Remote Areas
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Among the thousands of islands in Indonesia, there are few remote areas that have not installed telecommunication networks. This paper proposes a simple, inexpensive and portable GSM telecommunications infrastructure in the form of OpenBTS with USRP N210 that can be applied in remote areas. Difficulties and failures of implementing OpenBTS usually occurred when compiling OpenBTS software. So this paper describes an experimental application of the GSM OpenBTS software version 5.0 on USRP N210. The dev/ build.sh and deb / libcoredumper / build.sh files were revised to avoid failing. Then, the new script letc/asterisk/extensions-custom.conf makes asterisk executable. Version 5.0 is more practical and easier to install, and the Asterik softswitch installation has been integrated into the OpenBTS software. Output of the experiment is a cheap and portable OpenBTS infrastructure which is used as a GSM radio transceiver at 900MHz (900.401 Mhz uplink and 945.401 MHz downlink). The result is 4 cellphones connected to the GSM system. Performance test on the experimental device is a coverage area of 25 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> for audio calls with a receiving power level of = -65 dB, and 75 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> for text messages with a power level of -80 dB.

articleTitle: Energy Management Applications in Battery And Supercapacitor Hybrid Electric Vehicles Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The battery is primarily used in electric vehicles as an energy storage unit because it has a large energy storage capacity. The disadvantages of the typical battery are that it has a small power density, a limited-service life, and a relatively high price. Due to the driving cycle characteristics of electric vehicles, which are often not constant, because an excessive charge-discharge process causes them, it decreases battery life. Additional energy storage systems such as the supercapacitor are recently applied to overcome energy fulfilment. Since the battery and the supercapacitor have different characteristics in charging and discharging operation, a proper energy management system should be applied. An intelligent method to share the energy consumption of both battery and supercapacitor is proposed in this research. This paper proposed a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) be applied to the power distribution control for the hybrid energy storage system. The proposed power distribution is carried out by attaching a buck converter to the battery. The duty cycle value of the buck converter is controlled using FLC according to vehicle starting, normal, and regenerative braking operation. The simulation uses MATLAB Simulink software. The simulation result shows that the FLC can successfully manage the energy sharing between the battery and supercapacitor according to vehicle operation when in the starting condition, the supercapacitor fully supplies the power demand. Under normal conditions, most of the power demand is supplied by the battery. Under the regenerative braking condition, the supercapacitor fully receives the current and power.

articleTitle: PV-Wind Hybrid System Design at the Tambakrejo Fisherman's Village in the Tamban Coastal Area Malang
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Tamban Beach, Tambakrejo Village, Sumbermanjing Wetan District, Malang Regency, East Java has the potential for wind and solar energy. And when viewed from the aspect of the geographical location of Tamban beach facing the Indian Ocean, wind energy is quite abundant in existence and solar energy can be obtained as long as the sun is still shining. The combination of two renewable energy potentials can be used for the electrification of Neayan Village, Tambakrejo Village. By utilizing various local energies such as wind and solar, it is hoped that dependence on commercial electrical energy can be reduced gradually. The on-grid PV-Wind hybrid system design consists of solar panels, converters, AC-DC buses, and wind turbines connected to the PLN grid. From the results of the analysis, the electricity production by the hybrid plant reaches 13.8 gW/year and the renewable fraction is 71.2%. And the emissions produced by the PV-Wind hybrid system on grid are 2,435,974 kg/year, which is smaller than that by PLN, which produces carbon dioxide of 5,757,283 kg/year. In addition, the on-grid PV-Wind hybrid system results in a lower cost per kWh (C0E) of IDR 414.6.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Network Design in Enggano Island for Tourism Development Purposes
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Enggano Island is one of the beautiful small islands in Bengkulu Province that many tourists visit. Unfortunately, the island has no connection to a fiber optic network. Internet connectivity is an important requirement, with the internet being an important part of almost every step in life, specifically tourism. This paper discusses a proposed optical network design and analysis its feasibility for connecting Sumatera island with Enggano island. The considered parameters for analysis are power link loss and rise-time. The estimated link loss is not exceeding the determined value of 28 dB by applying an amplifier. Meanwhile, the obtained rise-time is 232.49 ps, which does not exceed the dispersion limit. Therefore, the proposed design can be a reference for further implementation.

articleTitle: Modified Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna to Gain Enhancement for Ultrawideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The utilization of the antenna as the supporting device for telecommunication infrastructure is essential, including its function for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. UWB needs ultra-wideband antennas. One of the antennas is an Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (AVA). This paper presents a modified AVA to enhance the gain by adding a trapezoidal dielectric director (TDD). The TTD is placed in the direction of wave propagation to amplify receiving of the EM waves. A characteristic of the proposed antenna has been simulated. The result shows that the proposed antenna achieves return loss> 10 dB at the 3.6 GHz - 12 GHz frequency range with a better-matched impedance and more stability. This method also gave a better gain up to 11.81 dBi. This method also helps the antenna reduce a beam split on its main lobe at a high frequency.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Disc Coil for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Electricity transfer power in Indonesia is still very dependent on fossil energy. It has prompted a lot of research on electric cars. One of these studies is about charging electric vehicles. A new strategy for charging electric vehicles is to use a wireless system. This system can be called wireless power transfer (WPT). So in this research, a wireless power transfer coil disc is made without a ferrite core. This disc coil WPT uses a series resonance coupling. The frequency used in this study is 100kHz, generated by Arduino Uno R3. The results in this study have the optimal distance of electrical power that can be transferred is 9 cm. The efficiency of the disk coil WPT in this study was 50.27%.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Analysis of Wireless Access Point (WAP) and Virtual Access Point (VAP) Based on Mikrotik at SD Negeri 01 Jambearjo
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The development of internet technology currently has a significant impact on education, so that it can support the learning process in a school. As one of the public schools in Malang district, SD Negeri 01 Jambearjo has utilized the internet network to support the learning process at school. However, the use of the internet network at SD Negeri 01 Jambearjo is currently still not optimized. This study discusses the comparative analysis of the performance of Mikrotik-based Wireless Access Point (WAP) and Virtual Access Point (VAP) at SD Negeri 01 Jambearjo. This research was conducted to find out which system is better to use in SD Negeri 01 Jambearjo. The WAP and VAP network systems are used by Mikrotik RB941-2nD to configure or control access points centrally. In the WAP network, an access point is used that is connected to the Mikrotik using a LAN cable, while the VAP network uses the CAPsMAN mode which combines two Mikrotik RB941-2nD with a LAN cable. The testing process uses parameters based on Quality of Service, including throughput, packet loss, delay, and jitter. In the Quality of Service test, the Wireshark application is used. The test results on the WAP network obtained an average throughput value of 3034 kbps, with packet loss of 3.16%, delay of 2.840 ms, and jitter of 0 ms. While on the VAP network, the average throughput value is 1479 kbps, with packet loss of 9.9%, delay of 4.945 ms, and jitter of 0.0011 ms. Based on the test results, the analysis results show that the WAP network has better quality than the VAP network for use in SD Negeri 01 Jambearjo.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Li-Polymer Battery Using Non-Linear Feedback Structure Aproximation
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an accurate battery model which can be implemented easily in the real time parameter estimation of an Li-Polymer cell. An equivalent circuit-based battery model with nonlinear feedback structure is proposed. The relationship between the open circuit voltage and the state-of-charge parameter is represented by some non-linear components. The developed battery model is purposed to be used for the implementation of a parameter estimation algorithm on a microcontroller-based application. Parameters estimation consists of two execution processes, being aimed to find the time constant and the steady-state gain of the first-order parts and to find the parameters of the relaxation effect of the battery. The parameters are updated continuously for each of the three input pulses of current. The proposed method and model are then verified in real time application of Li-Pol batteries.

articleTitle: 5G NR Network Planning in Malang City East Java Using Atoll Software
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Telecommunications network technology has entered the fifth generation or often called 5G NR. The availability of 5G NR network services is expected to be a solution to improve the quality of telecommunication networks in Malang City. The research discusses the planning of the 5G NR network in the city of Malang. A 5G network at a frequency of 28 GHz and a bandwidth of 100 MHz is simulated with the Atoll software. 5G network planning is done by calculating the need for gNodeB in the city of Malang. The number of gNodeB is obtained by analysis of coverage dimensioning and capacity dimensioning. The gNodeB obtained is simulated in the city of Malang using Atoll software to obtain the coverage area parameters. 5G network planning in the city of Malang using Atoll software is able to predict customer needs in the next five years.

articleTitle: Implementation of High Voltage Converter Circuit Based on Transformer Switching Method for Biphasic and Monophasic External Defibrillator
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: High voltage converter on external defibrillator was built using transformer switching method. An input of 12V DC supply voltage was converted to a maximum 2000V. The voltage conversion result was used for energy charging process of storage capacitors. The proposed defibrillator can adjust the energy by changing duty cycle of the Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signal on Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT). In this case, IGBT is used to control the current and voltage in the transformer. The maximum energy generated by the conversion process is 500 joules and has met the requirement of the defibrillation. In addition, this device was designed to discharge energy in both biphasic and monophasic modes. The mode can be set according to the needs of the defibrillation process.

articleTitle: Fuel Cell Penetration Characteristics on Standalone Photovoltaic with Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In the renewable energy area, the lack of power stability aspects seen from the response to changes when there is an intermittency of the input. Fuel cell is proven to be able to dampen the response. But, by using the modified standalone with hybrid energy storage system, the fuel cell penetration effect has to be evaluated before the system goes through in the field. The purpose of this paper is to provide the fuel cell, using PEMFC model, penetration characteristics on standalone photovoltaic with hybrid energy storage system. From the results, the characteristics obtained that fuel cell penetration give the better result in power quality aspect, and got its power stability during the injection to the system. The supercapacitor in the hybrid storage system the contribution to dampen the injection effect, but give the less contribution to power distribution, and the load had sustained at nearly zero or safe injection effect during fuel cell power injection.

articleTitle: A Fast Electrical Distribution Fault Predictor using Knowledge Growing System (KGS)
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Electrical energy is one of important needs in our everyday life from the household to the industries and increases day by day. Any disruption to the electrical distribution will disrupt its reliability that impacts to the electrical supply to various sectors. Such situation has often occurred at State Electrical Company (SEC) unit of Lambung Mangkurat in Borneo Island. Predicting the electrical distribution fault that causes the disruption can be carried out in advance to reduce the problem of electrical supply. For this purpose, we propose a new fast prediction technique called Knowledge Growing System (KGS) to predict the electrical distribution fault. KGS is an intelligent agent that can generate its own knowledge regarding a phenomenon it is observing and uses the generated knowledge to make predictions. By having knowledge about 11 electrical fault patterns at the electrical distribution site, KGS has able to predict that the most probable fault to occur is Fault Short-circuited Primary Coil Burned (FSPCB) with the probability of 0.2830. With a fast prediction, the SEC unit can develop a proper plan to cope with the fault and to recover the electrical supply quicker.

articleTitle: Recognition of Radiographic Weld Defects based on Combining ResNet18 and Q-learning for Imbalanced Train Dataset
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low generalization ability and accuracy under imbalanced train dataset of identifying weld defects of radiographic images, the improved resnet18 deep neural networks combining q-learning algorithm was proposed. in this method, five types of weld defects images were enhanced as the datasets including slag inclusion, gas pore, crack, lack of fusion and non-defects. Q-learning algorithm was proposed to identify the types of weld defects and a personalized reward function was constructed for the imbalanced ratio (IMR) of the training set. The improved ResNet18 network was designed to extract weld defects images features deeply. The agent used the weld defects images as the current state and five types of defects were used as an agent action. The agent performed recognition actions at each time step and return the value. Finally, the network learned the strategy of weld defects recognition under IMR train dataset. The experimental results showed that the improved ResNet18 network with Q-learning algorithm had good generalization ability, for the extremely imbalanced dataset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(IMR=1/9)$</tex>. The recall rate still reached over 92% and the accuracy rate reached over 87% and the precision rate over 90%.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation GUI for 50 MW Large Scale Solar PV System
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Performance Ratio is one of important criteria to evaluate the achievement of Large Scale Solar Photovoltaic Power Plant. An establishment of graphic user interface tools for estimate the performance of Large Scale Solar Photovoltaic is developed for future economical and monitoring system purposes. This paper presents the performance evaluation system using Visual Basic software to create a graphic user interface platform and the comprehensive design of Large Scale Solar Photovoltaic system modeled using Matlab Simulink to evaluates the performance ratio using real-time data extracted from real-time 50 MW LSSPV power plant site. The data is extracted from real-time meteorological station and automatically generated from Large Scale Solar Photovoltaic plant and compared with PV syst designed report. The system is successfully simulated where the performance ratio of 50MW Kuala Ketil Large Scale Solar Photovoltaic modelled in Matlab Simulink provides a modulation index at VSC with 85% while the evaluation of PR based on GUI are obtained at 82% and 83% on March and April respectively. An established performance evaluation system for large-scale solar power plant is a crucial approach to measure the quality of the electricity generation from the plant.

articleTitle: Quadcopter Design With Waypoint Mission Using PID Control System
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The quadcopter is one of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicles that can fly vertically. Problems with the drone such as unresponsive controls and choosing the right control system which has an impact on the instability of the drone. Proportional, Integral, Derivative (PID) has better performance to be applied to the quadcopter. This study applies PID control to the quadcopter control which is tested with a waypoint system. Quadcopter design uses various components such as flight controller, brushless motor 920 kv, electronic speed controller. The results of the calculation of the constant PID value are applied to the drone flight controller and the test is carried out by carrying out a waypoint tracking mission with the PID controller. Testing with a rectangular route waypoint shows that the quadcopter can fly according to the predetermined waypoint with the largest roll deviation value is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20.93^{o}$</tex>, at pitch by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24.01^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex>, and the largest deviation change at yaw is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$205^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> which means the quadcopter can carry out waypoint tracking missions using PID control with high stability.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating Soil Water Content in The Presence of Vegetation Using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In agriculture and plantations, soil water content significantly affects growth, productivity, and sustainability. Soil water content is important information for agriculture and plantation. Direct measurement of soil water content, such as the gravimetric method on large areas, requires time and cost. The remote sensing technology can potentially be applied for measuring a large area. Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) has been studied to measure soil water content. However, the presence of vegetation can act as an obstacle and significantly influence the detection results. This influence can cause a decrease in the accuracy of the detection results. Therefore, the presence of vegetation needs to be considered in estimating the soil water content. This paper proposes an extraction method for estimating soil water content considering the presence of vegetation. The proposed method is applied for the Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) system employed as a radar system used in soil water content estimation. The theoretical and simulation analysis was conducted to investigate the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method overcomes the problem of vegetation in soil water content estimation. The accuracy improvement that obtains is about 4.248%. The proposed method also performs well in the low SNR condition.

articleTitle: Cache Size Effects and Content Request in Spatially Dispersed Caching Strategy
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The design of Information-Centric Networking (ICN) technology aims to create a reliable network that can meet the present and future needs. Nowadays, almost every aspect of data exchanges uses the internet, which the ICN is an important technology for the internet. One of the strategic models for ICN have been created is Spatially Dispersed Caching (SDC). Thus, this strategy, groups content based on unique names to dispersed spatially. And, the more popular content will be cached in many routers. Finally, in this study will further deepen the SDC strategy and analyze the cache hit values by changing the value of several parameters, namely the number of users, cache size, and content requests. In addition, have been found that the parameter more effect on the cache hit is the cache size, where the increase in cache size correlates by 45% against the increase in a cache hit. While the increase in the number of users and content requests only have a proportion of the increase in cache hits by 22% and 32%. Meanwhile, the effect of the number of users, cache size, and content requests on cache hits is fixed even though it has been experimented by changing the topology, but for the results of path stretch, topology changes have an effect where the second topology with average value 1.76 will always be better than the first topology with average value 2.7 because the second topology has two nodes that are directly connected to the user so that it will make content delivery more effective.

articleTitle: Effect of Radar-Drone Elevation Stability on Estimation Soil Water
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The implementation of radar-drone for soil water content (SWC) data mapping in plantation areas found the plant height variations that caused the fluctuation in radar drones elevation. The stability of the radar-drone elevation is needed to ensure the SWC estimation results from the radar have good accuracy. The drone's altitude control system proposes pre- processing of Lidar data to overcome this problem. The Autoregressive Moving Average (ARMA) structure was studied and proposed as a Lidar data pre-processing method for generating the drone flight controller input. Simulation studies and experiments on tea plantations have been carried out. The results obtained indicate that the proposed method can improve the accuracy of the SWC estimation of the radar-drone system.

articleTitle: IoT Monitoring and Control System for Smart Cage Turtledove Bird
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Currently, one of the most popular and rapidly growing businesses as well as hobbies in Indonesia is become a turtledove bird breeder. It recorded in the P3SI institution that the number of registered turtledove breeders has reached more than 2000 breeders. In this number, almost all breeders still carry out conventional breeding treatments which take a long time. In this paper, proposed a smart birdcage using the ESP8266 module and automatic temperature control by STM32F4 discovery. The integration of IoT can help breeders manage all of the cages and the turtledoves birds can grow optimal. The smart cage use temperature and light Dependent Sensors (LDR). The outputs are dc motors, and exhaust fans control with the Internet of Things (IoT). Meanwhile, the cage heating control system uses the PI control method to adjust the PWM on the AC module control for the brightness level of incandescent lamps. In this research, author choose PI control because temperature does not have an overshot as same as starting current in motor. So, derivative control is not needed. The expected result of this proposal is to help old or busy turtledove breeders monitor the cages at any time and be more efficient.

articleTitle: Perception Modeling of In-Pipe Robot based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: During the pipeline detection of the in-pipe robot, obstacles such as welds inside the pipeline will interfere with the movement of the robot. It can result in changes of the flow field environment around the robot. Its velocity and attitude can also change, making the errors of pipeline defect positioning. And it cannot meet the detection requirements. Therefore, a perception model of the in-pipe robot's drive system was established. It can adjust the driving torque in real time by sensing the velocity of the external flow field, the velocity and the attitude of the robot. And then the motion state of the robot can be adjusted to better adapt to the changes of the external environment. First, a composite-driven in-pipe robot was designed. And the dynamic analysis of the in-pipe robot was carried out to calculate the driving torque under different combinations of fluid velocities, velocities of robot motion and attitude angles. An offline database was constructed. Second, support vector regression (SVR) method was used to establish the prediction model of drive system. And the hyperparameters of the model were optimized through double deep Q-network (Double DQN) to improve the prediction performance. Finally, the optimal model parameters were selected through the comparison between the different parameters of the model. The results showed that the prediction error of the established perception model was controlled within 10<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</inf>, which improved the accuracy of the pipeline detection.

articleTitle: Frequency Variation on Grounding Rod with Additive Biochar and Fly-Ash
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The resistance of a grounding rod is largely determined by the conductivity of the soil layer closest to the rod electrode. By replacing the soil layer using another layer that has a smaller resistivity, the grounding rod resistance value can be significantly reduced. Biochar and fly-ash additives with lower resistivity than the soil can be used as a substitute layer to reduce the resistance value of the grounding rod. As a filler layer, biochar and fly-ash will be mixed in several compositions. A certain sinusoidal current with a frequency variation of up to 50kHz is injected into the grounding rod arrangement for each biochar and fly-ash composition, the voltage between the rod electrode and the auxiliary electrode is measured and the response is determined. The grounding rod response with a certain frequency can be determined from the recording of current and voltage waves on a two-channel oscilloscope. The grounding rod's response at a certain frequency can exhibit resistive, capacitive, or inductive properties.

articleTitle: VOLT/VAR Support from Unlicensed Solar Power Plants Integrated in Distribution Grid: YEDAS Pilot Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Due to the latest developments and financial opportunities in photovoltaic system (PV) investments in Turkey which results by renewable energy sources (RES) support mechanism, the rural areas installed capacity of unlicensed solar power plants has increased rapidly. Electricity distribution networks are designed to supply the energy from source to load. However due to these rapid increase in distributed generation (DG) connections, distribution system operator (DSO) is facing the inverse flow from load to the source. This transition of the nature of electrical grid phenomena brought a number of technical problems such as variation of feeder voltage and power factor. In this study, the contribution of DGs to solving these problems by using the existing capacity efficiently and economically.

articleTitle: Design Criteria of Distribution Transformer Using Graphic User Interface (GUI) based on Load Growth in 20 kV Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Electric power system planning is an important aspect to anticipate the increasing electricity demand each year. Therefore, it is necessary to plan electricity distribution networks such as planning for transformers and distribution substations that refer to existing conditions of the area as well as anticipated load growth to maintain optimal service. The ratings and capacity of the transformer are determined by long computations and intricate algorithms that can produce erroneous results in the current design standards for distribution transformers and distribution substations. This paper proposes to design a simulation program to bridge the issue using Graphic User Interface which can determine criteria of the transformer such as the ratings, the capacity, and the quantity of distribution transformer and distribution substation demanded in an area. The designed can accommodate load growth in algorithm calculation and the determination of the transformer rating still refers to the existing standards which must not exceed 80% of the transformer capacity. So it can reduce losses that may occur as a result of load requests that cannot be served and also optimize equipment, especially distribution transformers.

articleTitle: Soft Decision Decoding for Massive Sensor in Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In this research, we proposed a soft decision de-coding (SDD) using matched filters on the receiving side for Internet of Things (IoT) sensors in visible light communication (VLC). We simulated and analyzed the effect of Matched Filter on the distance between transmitter and receiver in a closed room. The information signal as bits has been modulated using on-off keying Non return to zero (OOK-NRZ) modulation before entering the Light Emitting Diode (LED) lights to be transmitted. The photodiode captured the light and converted it to an electrical signal. We employed SDD to enhance the decoding process from received signals. We consider several parameters to compare performance without a matched filter using a 100 Mbps bit-rate, the number of bits is 1 million bits, and the room size is 3x3x5 m. Also, we evaluated performance using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and bit error rate (BER) to compare decoding in the receiver. From the extensive simulation, the results show that maximum receiver coverage is 0.1414 m2 for direct decoding. When the matched filter system is added, we found that the coverage area increases to 0.7697 m2. In addition, SDD using matched filter has an improvement of around 43.5% in terms of coverage, so massive sensors are able to serve optimally.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensors Using Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) phenomenon of metamaterial have been observed using a modified Kretschmann configuration. The observation was carried out through simulation Ansys Lumerical software and compared with some experimental data refractive index (n), absorbance index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\kappa)$</tex>, and thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau)$</tex> reported in other literatures. This simulation assumed that the SPR system use SF-10 prism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{n}= 1,723$</tex>) and the laser beam was generated by He-Ne <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda=632,8$</tex> nm). The result showed that the optimum layer thickness of metamaterial with the additional of Gold, Copper, and Silver is of about 150 nm. The metamaterial with the additional of these materials showed that the reflectivity curve is sharper and the width of the curve is smaller than the neutral electrolyte solution in the reduction state with the SPR angle of about 44.80 and the reflectivity value of about 0,015. Metamaterial with the additional of other materials, related to the absorption, film thickness, and dielectric constant of materials, affected to the SPR angle shift and dip curve.

articleTitle: Implementation of PVWatts Software for Design of Roof Solar Panels at the Faculty of Engineering, Subang University
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The potential of solar energy in Subang reaches 4.8 kWh/m2. Subang University has potential in the development of solar energy and a Solar Power Plant study was conducted in the Faculty of Engineering building. In this study, it was found that from the results of PVWatts Software imaging at the Faculty of Engineering, the production of rooftop solar panel electrical energy was 10kWp in one year of 12,381kWh. This electrical energy can reduce the use of 64.71% of the energy consumption in the building.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Floating PV System at Sigura-Gura Hydropower Dam in North Sumatera, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The Floating Photovoltaic (FPV) is one of PV system applications that has several advantages, such as saving land cost and hybrid connection with existing hydropower system. FPV system application would support the expansion of the solar energy sector. This work simulates studies on the possibility of FPV system implementation in the existing dam in Sigura-Gura, North Sumatera, Indonesia. The objective of the work is to estimate the capacity of the PV system that can be installed and the amount of energy output of FPV system. Simulation is done using Google Erath and PVGIS software. The total water surface area of the dam was found to be around 233,964 m2, and about 12.6 MWp capacity solar modules are possible to be installed. With this FPV system capacity, the annual energy production is about 16.32 GWh. The FPV system can be hybridized with the existing hydropower plant.

articleTitle: Configuration of Inverted-V Dipole NVIS HF Antenna for Offshore Fast Patrol Boat
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: This paper describes the configuration of Inverted-V half-wave dipole antenna which was designed, simulated and deployed for offshore ship-patrol of a 28 Meter class Fast Patrol Boat (FPB) for its High Frequency (HF) communication system. The antenna is used for medium range of HF radio coverage by Near Vertical Incidence Skywave (NVIS) mode for sea to port and sea to sea communication scheme for radius around 300 kilometers. The effect of sea surface and ship's hull material on the radiation pattern was studied. Furthermore, the antenna height and the V-shape angle configuration were determined to compromise between the limited space, maximum antenna gain as well as its Standing Wave Ratio (SWR) value. The Numerical Electromagnetics Code (NEC) computer simulation describes not only the flat-bottomed radiation pattern due to high conductivity of the sea surface but also the 3-dB gain of the vertical main lobe as the typical characteristic of V-inverted dipole antenna. Designed antenna has the SWR value as low as 1.16 at 42-meter band with 40-degree angle of inverted V-shaped mounted on boat with 10 meters tall of mast above sea level coupled with a 100-Watt ICOM HF radio.

articleTitle: Automatic Garbage Classification System using Arduino-Based Controller and Binary Tree Concept
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: As Indonesia's population grows, the daily amount of garbage in landfills also increases. Effective garbage classification can maximize the utilization of garbage resources, reduce the amount of garbage disposal, improve the quality of living environment, and reduce the groundwater pollution from garbage. This research aims to design an automatic garbage classification system that use Arduino as a microcontroller and binary tree concept algorithm. The proposed design consists of automatic door, garbage sorter, user interface, and capacity observer. The main components of the system are Microcontroller Arduino Mega 2560, ultrasonic sensor HCSR04, servo motor MG996R, Inductive Proximity Sensor, and Capacitive Proximity Sensor. From the performance test result we can obtain that HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor as an object detector has an error in distance stabilization of 33.3%, inductive proximity sensors as metal detectors have a 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> success rate, while capacitive proximity sensors as organic garbage detector has a success rate of 85.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. Overall, the system has a success rate of 86.6% to classify various garbage from 30 experiments using the concept of binary tree in automatic garbage classification.

articleTitle: Multi-Point Small Displacement Detection of Bridge using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) is a method to monitor the condition of building structures that is useful for detecting damage as early as possible, which is also usually done on bridges. The SHM method using a non-contact sensor is proposed in this study. SHM is done by detecting small displacements using the Radar system. The type of FMCW Radar proposed in the study. FMCW radar is a type of radar that emits a continuous transmission signal that can be implemented on SHM on the bridges, because it can reduce spectrum usage so it is easy to implement. In this paper, a simulation study is conducted in developing a small displacement detection method on the bridge structure with multi-point detection feature using FMCW Radar. The phase data extraction technique was proposed to estimate the small displacement of several points over the bridge. The results show that the proposed method can detect multi-point displacement and provide the estimation of small displacement profile of the bridge. In addition, the study on noise effect on the detection performance has also been performed. The average error value is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.8\times 10^{-4}$</tex>. The noise has less significant effect on the detection performed.

articleTitle: Predictive Control Model for Identify Failure Between Sensor and Actuator on Engine Turbofan
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The research describes the design of a basic mathematical model using a nonlinear system with 6 degrees of freedom, where the system is smoothed into lateral and longitudinal dynamic flight modes in aircraft systems. To achieve a special transient performance of longitudinal and lateral dynamics modes, a strategy process is needed to design a predictive control model. The predictive control model scheme created in this research can be implemented on aircraft with 6 degrees of freedom. The simulation was conducted using Matlab/Simulink. The results showed that aircraft systems using predictive control models captured good transient performance. The research used the Kalman Filter Technique to identify recognize and separate errors between sensors and actuators on the aircraft's turbofan engine. Mathematic models of two turbofan engine shafts are made on Matlab/Simulink. Kalman filters are structured to determine certain speculations as identifying problems contained in the sensor. At the point where something goes wrong, all channels use proper speculation and will provide high estimated values of speculation.

articleTitle: Application of Modified P & O Algorithm using Current Deviation in Buck Converter for Damping Oscillation
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Solar energy is a renewable energy that can be transformed into electrical energy using solar modules. Solar energy efficiency is not optimal because it has non-linear characteristics when irradiation, temperature, and load are shifted. Therefore, solar modules require electronic technology to enhance the power generated. In order to obtain optimal power, the system requires a Maximum Power Point Tracker (MPPT), which includes an algorithm to track the maximum power of a PV module. Several algorithms are used in the MPPT system. The Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm is the most straightforward, but the given response when the irradiation change is not excellent. The modified P &O algorithm employs parameters dI and B to maximize the output power. The DC converter in this system uses a buck converter. Two model systems are tested: a system with a P&O algorithm and a modified P&O algorithm with irradiation testing. The simulation results show that the two algorithms can improve the output power. The P&O and proposed algorithms have an efficiency of around 87% when irradiation changes, producing more significant power. The output power yielded by the proposed algorithm has slight oscillations and delivers more significant power when there is various irradiation.

articleTitle: Optimization of Location, Capacity, and Number of UPFC in the 150 kV SUMBAGUT Transmission System by Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: In 2019, the power losses in the northern Sumatra 150 kV network system (SUMBAGUT) were 132.58 MW or 11.33% of the distributed power, in addition to the number of frequency disturbances per customer, which was 18.93 times. Based on these problems, it is necessary to repair the electrical system to increase its reliability. One of the factors assessing the electrical system's reliability can be seen from the voltage profile and power losses. To maintain the voltage profile and to reduce power losses, it is possible to install a Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC). So this study chose the optimal location, capacity, and number of UPFCs on the 150 kV SUMBAGUT transmission system using Particle Swarm Optimization. After optimizing the UPFC with 17 units and each capacity of 150 MVAR in various locations, the results were. Meanwhile, the voltage profile is at the PLN standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(+ 5{\%}$</tex>, -10%), and the power flow losses are 73.63 MW (44.46<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>).

articleTitle: Dual Band Absorber Based on Multilayer SSR
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The need to protect telecommunications equipment from electromagnetic wave interference is increasing rapidly with technology development. This paper proposes an absorber based on AMC that can eliminate EM waves, which are expected in dual-band of 2.4 GHz and 3.7 GHz. The proposed metamaterial absorber is expected to achieve multiband bandwidth by using a square split ring resonator multilayer with the square patch on the top layer. The type of unit cell is SRR which has the advantage of a simple shape and can produce a resonant frequency depending on the number of rings and various changes on the split or gap. To provide wide bandwidth is using multilayer technique with adding air gap between split-ring resonator on the bottom layer and square patch as a compliment on the top layer. Characterizing the parameter is tested by a series of computer simulations, which is realized with dimensions of 132mm x 132mm. The proposed design work well based on the range 2.37 GHz - 2.42 GHz and 3.65 GHz - 4.3 GHz with an absorptivity rate above 90% on return loss minimum value at -10 dB. The absorptivity rate at 2.4 GHz is 96%, and 3.7 GHz is 98%.

articleTitle: Tuning LQR Parameters using Neuro Evolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT) on a Double Pendulum Cart
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The double pendulum cart is an example of an unstable and nonlinear system. The modeling of this system can be done using the Euler-Lagrange method with linearization using Taylor Series expansion. Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) is one of the optimal control techniques applied to this problem. However, the process of tuning the Q and R matrices on the LQR is often made by design. This paper proposes LQR tuning method using Neuro Evolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT) to ensure that the system response has good stability, cost and gain feedback that is adaptive to the state value of the system. In this paper, the best genome produced through the NEAT process scored 31.1 from the designed objective function.

articleTitle: Dielectric Strength of $\text{SF}_{6}-\mathrm{N}_{2}$ and $\text{SF}_{6}-\text{CO}_{2}$ due to Temperature and Pollutants
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: SF <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> is the gas most used as an insulating medium in high voltage equipment. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF} _6$</tex> gas is categorized as a gas that can affect the greenhouse effect and global warming. So, a lot of research has been done to get other insulating materials as a substitute for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_6$</tex> This research is to determine the effect of temperature and pollutants on the dielectric strength of the gas mixture of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}-\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}-\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> using spherical electrodes with a diameter of 5cm at a pressure of 1 bar. The results showed that the dielectric strength of the insulating gas mixture decreased with increasing temperature and the influence of the presence of pollutants. Gas mixture 20% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_6$</tex> - 80% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{2}$</tex> has the best dielectric strength with pollutants, and without pollutants, at an initial temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{0}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, it is 98.03 kV/cm to 53.88 kV /cm, respectively. Furthermore, a mixture of 15% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_{6}-85\%$</tex> N2 at an initial temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{o}\mathrm{C}$</tex> is 92.35 kV/cm to 53.88 kV/cm with pollutants. On the other hand, a mixture of 20% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_6$</tex> - 80% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_2$</tex> at an initial temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{0}\mathrm{C}$</tex> was 82.59 kV/cm to 54.69 kV/cm. Finally, a mixture of 15% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_6$</tex> - 85% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_2$</tex>, at an initial temperature of 30°C, was 72.83 kV/cm to 51.89 kV/cm with pollutants.

articleTitle: Effect of Step Skewing on the Cogging Torque of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) is a generator whose magnetic field is generated by a permanent magnet located on the rotor and which does not require any external excitation source to generate the magnetic field. Although permanent magnet machines are high performance electric machines, there is a torque component that affects their output performance, being called cogging torque. Cogging torque also creates torque ripple during operation which also causes other disadvantages such as reduced efficiency, noise, and vibration in the system. To overcome the cogging problem, this research offers a step-skewing method. The purpose is to reduce the value of the change in reluctance with respect to position. A change in the axial dimension design of the rotor will reduce the value of the change in reluctance in the circumferential direction and thus the cogging torque will be reduced. The effect of the step-skewing in reducing the cogging torque on a permanent magnet synchronous generator is to be examined using 3D simulation using finite-element method (FEM) based software. Step skewing method is applied by varying the magnetic segments (j) parameter into 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7. The results show that the step-skewing method is effective in reducing the cogging torque on the permanent magnet synchronous generator. The greater the number of magnetic segments (j), the smaller the cogging torque value.

articleTitle: Design and Build an Environmental Conditioning System on a Smart Growth Box for Microgreens
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: An environmental conditioning system is a system capable of conditioning the environment on the Smart Growth Box device. In this study, the design of an environmental conditioning system was carried out which aims to control the parameters of air temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and light intensity in the Smart Growth Box. In this design, the DHT22 sensor is used for the detection of air temperature and humidity, a capacitive soil moisture sensor as a moisture detector for planting media, and LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) as a light intensity detector. The readings from the sensor will be processed by the ESP32 microcontroller to control the actuator. Air temperature and humidity parameters are conditioned by exhaust fan, soil moisture is conditioned by sprayer pump and automatically turns on the grow light LED (Light Emitting Diode) when the light intensity is less than the setpoint. This system can reduce the temperature by half a degree with the average length of time of 01:14 minutes, reduce humidity by 1% RH with the average length of time of 17:57 minutes, and increase the level of soil moisture by 7.71% with once watering and can automatically turn on the grow light LED when the light intensity less than 10 lux. This system is also able to increase the growth of microgreens with the results of microgreens growing more evenly, wider leaves, taller stems, and increasing crop yields.

articleTitle: A Review of Various Quantum Routing Protocols Designed for Quantum Network Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The quantum internet is a global system also called the future internet and is considered a complement to the classical packet switching internet, which performs the function of exchanging messages in the network in an innovative way, as it depends on the basic principles of quantum bits. In order to prepare for the quantum internet, its protocols must be configured initially like routing protocols, and because routing in the quantum internet depends mainly on the property of quantum entanglement, it is facing a constant challenge to what the quantum properties impose, Accordingly, studies in this field continue to emerge, as proposals for protocols are renewed. Therefore, in this research, we present a comprehensive study of the recently proposed quantum routing protocols by classifying these protocols into two categories, the first deals with the routing metrics on which the protocol depends, while the other deals with the problem being solved through the routing protocol. It is shown that although many metrics were suggested for routing protocols, the common metric was the throughput (entanglement rate), In addition, it was considered an essential metric in solving most of the routing problems in quantum networks.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Networks Connectivity based on Sensors Transmission Power
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: The efficiency to which a wireless multi sensor network is connected is generally measured by the probability that all the nodes are connected to a sink node (base station) via other intermediate nodes. Network connectivity represents a measure of how easily and reliably a packet sent by a node can reach another node in a network. This paper is aimed to find the connectivity measurement between the nodes in a wireless sensor network. The result is investigated by randomly deploying all the nodes in a given area and estimating the connectivity of the whole network. Achieving the simulation results from this work, it can be a contribution to the research in the measure of connectivity for a wireless sensor network. By using an available routing algorithm, an appropriate connectivity threshold is calculated to enhance the life time of the whole network. Various results and solutions are provided and discussed by different simulation experiments. The collected simulation results are utilized mathematically in generating a general formula to be used in advance to calculate any required parameter instead of re-running the simulation experiments. Different specific equations are proposed and created based on the regression fundamentals for each case. These equations are trained to find the simulation results. The training requirements are performed for all the results tables contents and some examples are considered in this paper results. The equations results are found very accurate and identical with the simulation results. These equations can be easily used to calculate any wanted result without running the simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis Patch Stack Microstrip Antenna for Low Elevation of Mobile Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance analysis of patch stack six patches as receiver and transmitter become one configuration of triangular microstrip array antenna both simulation and measurement results at low elevation, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{El}=48^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> and at frequency target 2.5025 GHz and 2.6575 GHz. In this time, we compare the receiver (Rx) and the transmitter (Tx) of this antenna, especially the values of frequency characteristic, input impedances, and radiation pattern. Also, we add the PET radome for Rx to be analyzed its effect toward the antenna performance. The method of moments is used considering an infinite ground analysis. The input impedances of this antenna in calculation and measurement both at 2.5025 GHz for Rx and at 2.6575 GHz for Tx are closed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50 \Omega$</tex> or about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$33.07+\mathrm{j}2.68\Omega$</tex> and about 35.17 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+\mathrm{i}1.79\Omega$</tex> and about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$32.02 + \mathrm{i}16.44 \Omega$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$31.2 +\mathrm{j}2.22\Omega$</tex>, respectively. Moreover, the radiation pattern, especially the elevation cut-plane at El <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=48^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> for six patches of Rx around 0.007 dB and 0.1 dB of axial ratio and 7.2 dBic and 7.1 dBic of gain. While for Tx about dB and 1.2 dB of axial ratio and 5.9 and 5.8 of gain. Moreover, when using a sized PET radome 22 x 11, the performance of antenna, especially the elevation angle which shift from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{El} =38^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{El }=58^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{f}=2.5025$</tex> GHz (Rx) yields the gain more than 5 dBic and the axial ratio less than 3 dB. Here, the antenna performance does not be affected in significant value.

articleTitle: Identification of AI-Related Topic Evolution Based on Extraction of International Conference Proceedings Titles
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
abstract: International conference proceedings are a forum for researchers in various parts of the world to communicate their research findings to the scientific community and to the public in general. International conference proceedings published by globally recognized institutions are of unquestionable quality. Every conference must have a title that describes the theme or topic being discussed. This study wants to reveal the topic evolution by extracting conference titles. This study collects conference titles that contain terms related to artificial intelligence (AI) in them. Then the titles that have been collected are extracted to obtain a base noun phrase and filtered to eliminate uninformative terms. Of the 139,495 conference titles, it was obtained 8,133 titles containing topics related to AI. The results of the title extraction are 4,601 terms which are dominated by the exact term ‘artificial intelligence’, followed by the terms ‘machine learning’, ‘applications’, ‘intelligent systems’, ‘semantic’, ‘pattern recognition’ and other important related terms. Based on the glossary, frequency of occurrence, and year of publication, further identification of the evolution of a more specific topic is presented in this study. This study identified the early emergence and evolutionary phases of topics for specific terms such as natural language processing, cloud computing, and cybernetics or cyber security. Using the model proposed in this study, the process of identifying the evolution of specific topic can be extracted to get new insights.

articleTitle: Analysis of Changes in Induction Motor Efficiency due to Voltage Changes and Defects in Cageball Using the Segregated Loss Method
publicationTitle: 2022 11th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
